claims.text: Chemical short-range order typically suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
The suppression occurs through enhanced phonon scattering rather than ordering-induced phonon coherence.
MoNbTaW is a body-centered-cubic refractory high-entropy alloy that can be represented as a random solid solution.
A disordered MoNbTaW solid solution has high configurational entropy.
The low lattice thermal conductivity of the disordered state is caused by mass-disorder scattering.
Controlled thermal annealing or related processing can induce SRO without producing long-range precipitates.
MoNbTaW can exhibit relatively strong SRO at 800 K while remaining above its long-range-ordering transition.
The relevant SRO transport regime for RHEAs is typically between 300 K and 1000 K.
SRO forms local B2-like or L12-like motifs that create atomic-scale periodic potential variations.
In the disordered state, phonons are scattered by mass variance and random strain fields.
SRO creates a periodic potential that can open phonon band gaps or increase Umklapp scattering at selected wavelengths.
A mismatch between the SRO correlation length and the dominant phonon mean free path enhances scattering.
The enhanced scattering reduces phonon mean free path and therefore reduces lattice thermal conductivity.
In MoNbTaW, SRO enhances edge-dislocation mobility but reduces the rate of double-kink nucleation governing screw-dislocation motion.
The SRO state should have measurably lower lattice thermal conductivity than the compositionally identical disordered state.
The magnitude of conductivity suppression depends on SRO strength and the phonon wavelength spectrum.
SRO-induced suppression is most pronounced at intermediate temperatures and is washed out by thermal vibrations at very high temperatures.
At sufficiently low temperature, matching the SRO correlation length to the phonon wavelength could enable coherent transmission and enhance conductivity.
The influence of SRO on MoNbTaW dislocation mobility becomes attenuated as temperature increases.
Higher or equal lattice thermal conductivity in the SRO sample relative to the disordered control is specified as the falsifying outcome.

contradictions.description: The boundary permits enhanced conductivity at sufficiently low temperature, whereas the experiment states without a temperature qualification that higher or equal conductivity in the SRO sample falsifies the hypothesis.
